sentence: 'While the nineteenth-century factory depended on local workers, its modern successor recruits internationally.'
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'while' in this comparison across different historical periods.
taskText: 'While the nineteenth-century factory depended on local workers, its modern successor recruits internationally.'
text: Choose the meaning of 'while' in this comparison across different historical periods. 'While the nineteenth-century factory depended on local workers, its modern successor recruits internationally.'
options: The two recruitment systems operated simultaneously.
The writer contrasts the recruitment patterns of the two organizations.
The earlier factory caused the modern firm to recruit internationally.
International recruitment occurred only during local recruitment.
answer: The writer contrasts the recruitment patterns of the two organizations.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-561:Contrastive while distinguished from temporal while
explanation: 'While' has a contrastive function here, comparable to 'whereas', rather than its temporal meaning.

rationales.The two recruitment systems operated sim: The periods are different; 'while' cannot describe literal simultaneity between them here.
rationales.The earlier factory caused the modern fi: The sentence compares the patterns without asserting a causal connection.
rationales.The writer contrasts the recruitment pat: 'While' has a contrastive function here, comparable to 'whereas', rather than its temporal meaning.
rationales.International recruitment occurred only: This imposes a time restriction on recruitment that the comparison does not express.

sentence: 'The trial showed a measurable, albeit modest, improvement.'
setupText: Choose the interpretation that preserves the scope of 'albeit'.
taskText: 'The trial showed a measurable, albeit modest, improvement.'
text: Choose the interpretation that preserves the scope of 'albeit'. 'The trial showed a measurable, albeit modest, improvement.'
options: The trial showed no measurable improvement.
The improvement was measurable, with its limited size acknowledged.
The trial was modest in size, but the improvement was substantial.
The improvement was measurable because it was modest.
answer: The improvement was measurable, with its limited size acknowledged.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-562:Albeit qualifies one aspect of a claim
explanation: 'Albeit' introduces a concession about the size of the measurable improvement.

rationales.The trial showed no measurable improveme: 'Albeit' qualifies the improvement; it does not cancel the claim that improvement was measured.
rationales.The improvement was measurable, with its: 'Albeit' introduces a concession about the size of the measurable improvement.
rationales.The trial was modest in size, but the im: 'Modest' modifies 'improvement', not 'trial', and does not support a substantial effect.
rationales.The improvement was measurable because i: The relation is concessive, not causal: modest size is not presented as the reason for measurability.

sentence: 'Higher attendance may reflect clearer reminders rather than greater enthusiasm.'
setupText: Choose the inference warranted by the cautious alternative explanation.
taskText: 'Higher attendance may reflect clearer reminders rather than greater enthusiasm.'
text: Choose the inference warranted by the cautious alternative explanation. 'Higher attendance may reflect clearer reminders rather than greater enthusiasm.'
options: The writer proposes reminders as an alternative explanation without establishing the cause.
Greater enthusiasm has been proved absent.
Clearer reminders definitely caused the higher attendance.
The two proposed explanations are asserted to contribute equally.
answer: The writer proposes reminders as an alternative explanation without establishing the cause.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-563:Tentative alternative explanation with may and rather than
explanation: May limits certainty while rather than puts the reminder explanation against the enthusiasm account.

rationales.Greater enthusiasm has been proved absen: Favoring a possible alternative explanation does not prove enthusiasm absent.
rationales.Clearer reminders definitely caused the: May keeps the explanation tentative rather than establishing causation.
rationales.The two proposed explanations are assert: Rather than contrasts the explanations; it does not assert equal contributions.
rationales.The writer proposes reminders as an alte: May limits certainty while rather than puts the reminder explanation against the enthusiasm account.

sentence: The survey is informative ___ it reveals residents' reported preferences; it does not establish what they will actually do.
setupText: Choose the connector restricting the claim to the aspect for which it is supported.
taskText: The survey is informative ___ it reveals residents' reported preferences; it does not establish what they will actually do.
text: Choose the connector restricting the claim to the aspect for which it is supported. The survey is informative ___ it reveals residents' reported preferences; it does not establish what they will actually do.
options: even though
insofar as
now that
so that
answer: insofar as
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-564:Insofar as restricts the respect in which a claim holds
explanation: Insofar as limits the survey's value to the specified respect, reported preferences.

rationales.insofar as: Insofar as limits the survey's value to the specified respect, reported preferences.
rationales.even though: Even though would cast revealing preferences as a concession rather than the basis and limit of usefulness.
rationales.now that: Now that emphasizes a new factual circumstance rather than restricting the scope of the claim.
rationales.so that: 'So that' expresses purpose, not the extent or respect in which the survey is informative.

sentence: The comparison is misleading ___ the two totals cover different periods, not because either total is inaccurate.
setupText: Choose the connector giving the stated basis for the criticism.
taskText: The comparison is misleading ___ the two totals cover different periods, not because either total is inaccurate.
text: Choose the connector giving the stated basis for the criticism. The comparison is misleading ___ the two totals cover different periods, not because either total is inaccurate.
options: inasmuch as
lest
even though
until
answer: inasmuch as
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-565:Inasmuch as identifies the basis of a judgment
explanation: 'Inasmuch as' introduces the respect or reason that makes the comparison misleading; the following clause excludes a different reason.

rationales.lest: Lest introduces an event to prevent, not an existing reason for criticism.
rationales.even though: Even though concedes the different periods rather than making them the stated basis of the criticism.
rationales.inasmuch as: 'Inasmuch as' introduces the respect or reason that makes the comparison misleading; the following clause excludes a different reason.
rationales.until: Until creates a time endpoint, which does not express the methodological criticism.

sentence: 'Much as I admire the proposal, I cannot recommend funding it at present.'
setupText: Choose the interpretation of 'much as' in this response.
taskText: 'Much as I admire the proposal, I cannot recommend funding it at present.'
text: Choose the interpretation of 'much as' in this response. 'Much as I admire the proposal, I cannot recommend funding it at present.'
options: The speaker cannot recommend it because admiration is absent.
The greater the admiration, the stronger the funding recommendation.
The speaker's admiration is genuine but does not lead to a funding recommendation.
Funding the proposal is the purpose of expressing admiration.
answer: The speaker's admiration is genuine but does not lead to a funding recommendation.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-566:Much as introduces an emphatic concession
explanation: The construction acknowledges admiration while contrasting it with the actual recommendation.

rationales.The speaker cannot recommend it because: 'Much as' concedes strong admiration rather than denying it.
rationales.The speaker's admiration is genuine but: The construction acknowledges admiration while contrasting it with the actual recommendation.
rationales.The greater the admiration, the stronger: This reads the clause as a proportional relation, but it is concessive here.
rationales.Funding the proposal is the purpose of e: The sentence states an evaluation and a contrasting decision, not a purpose for expressing praise.

sentence: 'Difficult as the negotiations were, both sides reached an agreement.'
setupText: Choose the rewrite preserving a concession, not a reason or an exact comparison.
taskText: 'Difficult as the negotiations were, both sides reached an agreement.'
text: Choose the rewrite preserving a concession, not a reason or an exact comparison. 'Difficult as the negotiations were, both sides reached an agreement.'
options: Although the negotiations were difficult, both sides reached an agreement.
The sides agreed because the negotiations were difficult.
Agreement was possible only while the negotiations remained difficult.
Negotiating and reaching agreement were equally difficult.
answer: Although the negotiations were difficult, both sides reached an agreement.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-567:Concessive adjective fronting with as
explanation: Fronted adjective + 'as' + subject + verb expresses concession here, equivalent to 'although'.

rationales.The sides agreed because the negotiation: Because makes difficulty the cause of agreement instead of a conceded obstacle.
rationales.Agreement was possible only while the ne: This turns a conceded obstacle into a necessary time condition for agreement.
rationales.Negotiating and reaching agreement were: This changes concessive as into a comparison of degrees of difficulty.
rationales.Although the negotiations were difficult: Fronted adjective + 'as' + subject + verb expresses concession here, equivalent to 'although'.

sentence: 'The moment the embargo was lifted, the researchers shared the dataset.'
setupText: Choose the meaning of 'the moment' as a connector.
taskText: 'The moment the embargo was lifted, the researchers shared the dataset.'
text: Choose the meaning of 'the moment' as a connector. 'The moment the embargo was lifted, the researchers shared the dataset.'
options: Sharing continued throughout the restriction.
Sharing caused the restriction to end.
The restriction ended after a lengthy delay in sharing.
Sharing began immediately when the restriction ended.
answer: Sharing began immediately when the restriction ended.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-568:A noun phrase functioning as a time connector
explanation: 'The moment' functions as a time connector meaning 'as soon as', emphasizing immediate sequence.

rationales.Sharing began immediately when the restr: 'The moment' functions as a time connector meaning 'as soon as', emphasizing immediate sequence.
rationales.Sharing continued throughout the restric: The clause locates sharing at the end of the restriction, not during it.
The sentence states timing, not that sharing caused the embargo to be lifted.
rationales.The restriction ended after a lengthy de: A lengthy delay contradicts the immediacy conveyed by 'the moment'.

sentence: No sooner had the negotiations ended ___ a new dispute arose.
setupText: Choose the completion following the conventional 'no sooner' construction in formal written English.
taskText: No sooner had the negotiations ended ___ a new dispute arose.
text: Choose the completion following the conventional 'no sooner' construction in formal written English. No sooner had the negotiations ended ___ a new dispute arose.
options: when
until
that
than
answer: than
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-569:No sooner ... than for rapid succession
explanation: 'No sooner ... than' connects two events occurring in rapid succession, with inversion in the first clause.

rationales.when: 'When' pairs with 'hardly' or 'scarcely' in the corresponding construction; 'no sooner' takes 'than'.
rationales.until: 'Until' marks a duration endpoint and does not complete 'no sooner' here.
rationales.than: 'No sooner ... than' connects two events occurring in rapid succession, with inversion in the first clause.
rationales.that: 'That' introduces other kinds of clauses, not the second event in this conventional pairing.

sentence: 'The names were removed lest participants be identified from the quotations.'
setupText: Choose the interpretation of the formal purpose clause.
taskText: 'The names were removed lest participants be identified from the quotations.'
text: Choose the interpretation of the formal purpose clause. 'The names were removed lest participants be identified from the quotations.'
options: Removal aimed to prevent identification, without reporting whether identification occurred.
Participants had already been identified, causing removal.
Removal was intended to make identification easier.
Identification was an unexpected fact conceded despite removal.
answer: Removal aimed to prevent identification, without reporting whether identification occurred.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-570:Lest expresses preventive purpose without asserting an event
explanation: Lest introduces the unwanted possibility that motivates the precaution; it does not report its realization.

rationales.Participants had already been identified: Lest states a feared outcome to prevent, not an established earlier identification.
rationales.Removal aimed to prevent identification,: Lest introduces the unwanted possibility that motivates the precaution; it does not report its realization.
rationales.Removal was intended to make identificat: This reverses the negative purpose: identification is what removal is meant to prevent.
rationales.Identification was an unexpected fact co: A lest-clause is preventive, not a concession asserting that the event happened.

sentence: 'The editor delayed naming the source for fear that disclosure might expose her to pressure.'
setupText: Choose the interpretation of the concern introduced by 'for fear that'.
taskText: 'The editor delayed naming the source for fear that disclosure might expose her to pressure.'
text: Choose the interpretation of the concern introduced by 'for fear that'. 'The editor delayed naming the source for fear that disclosure might expose her to pressure.'
options: The source had already faced pressure, and this established event caused the delay.
The delay was intended to put pressure on the source to agree to disclosure.
The editor regarded disclosure as inevitable and delayed only until the pressure ended.
Concern about possible pressure on the source motivated the delay.
answer: Concern about possible pressure on the source motivated the delay.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-571:For fear that introduces a motivating concern
explanation: The clause identifies an unconfirmed unwanted consequence as the reason for the editor's caution.

rationales.The source had already faced pressure, a: 'For fear that' with 'might' presents a feared possibility, not a reported event that has already happened.
rationales.The delay was intended to put pressure o: The feared pressure is an outcome the delay seeks to avoid, not the editor's intended goal.
rationales.Concern about possible pressure on the s: The clause identifies an unconfirmed unwanted consequence as the reason for the editor's caution.
rationales.The editor regarded disclosure as inevit: The sentence does not assert inevitable disclosure or define the delay by the end of actual pressure.

sentence: 'Granted that the service is cheaper, its limited opening hours make it unsuitable for our staff.'
setupText: Choose the function of 'granted that' in this argument.
taskText: 'Granted that the service is cheaper, its limited opening hours make it unsuitable for our staff.'
text: Choose the function of 'granted that' in this argument. 'Granted that the service is cheaper, its limited opening hours make it unsuitable for our staff.'
options: It leaves the price comparison entirely unresolved.
It gives low cost as the cause of limited opening hours.
It makes cheapness a guarantee of suitability.
It accepts the price advantage before challenging the overall suitability.
answer: It accepts the price advantage before challenging the overall suitability.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-572:Granted that as an argumentative concession
explanation: 'Granted that' concedes the favorable premise while allowing the main argument to reach a different overall judgment.

rationales.It accepts the price advantage before ch: 'Granted that' concedes the favorable premise while allowing the main argument to reach a different overall judgment.
rationales.It leaves the price comparison entirely: The speaker accepts the price advantage for the argument rather than leaving it unresolved.
rationales.It gives low cost as the cause of limite: The connector does not claim that lower cost causes the hours limitation.
rationales.It makes cheapness a guarantee of suitab: The main clause explicitly rejects suitability despite the lower cost.

sentence: 'The document refers to an event in 1998; hence, the claim that it was written in 1995 is doubtful.'
setupText: Choose the relationship signaled by 'hence'.
taskText: 'The document refers to an event in 1998; hence, the claim that it was written in 1995 is doubtful.'
text: Choose the relationship signaled by 'hence'. 'The document refers to an event in 1998; hence, the claim that it was written in 1995 is doubtful.'
options: The reference physically caused the document to be written later.
The date claim caused the document to mention the event.
The reference supplies evidence for questioning the claimed date.
The two dates describe successive stages of publication.
answer: The reference supplies evidence for questioning the claimed date.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-573:Hence for an evidential conclusion
explanation: 'Hence' introduces a conclusion supported by the discrepancy between the reference and the proposed date.

rationales.The reference physically caused the docu: The sentence draws an inference about dating, not a causal account of the writing process.
rationales.The date claim caused the document to me: This reverses the evidential direction and invents a cause of the reference.
rationales.The two dates describe successive stages: The writer questions a claim; no two-stage publication history is stated.
rationales.The reference supplies evidence for ques: 'Hence' introduces a conclusion supported by the discrepancy between the reference and the proposed date.

sentence: The sample is small. ___, the repeated pattern across all three sites deserves investigation.
setupText: Choose the continuation marker that resists the inference suggested by the first sentence.
taskText: The sample is small. ___, the repeated pattern across all three sites deserves investigation.
text: Choose the continuation marker that resists the inference suggested by the first sentence. The sample is small. ___, the repeated pattern across all three sites deserves investigation.
options: Accordingly
For that reason
Nevertheless
In other words
answer: Nevertheless
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-574:Nevertheless counters an implied conclusion
explanation: Nevertheless acknowledges the limitation while maintaining that the pattern merits attention.

rationales.Accordingly: Accordingly presents the recommendation as following from smallness, rather than resisting its discouraging implication.
rationales.Nevertheless: Nevertheless acknowledges the limitation while maintaining that the pattern merits attention.
rationales.For that reason: For that reason makes small sample size the reason to investigate the pattern.
rationales.In other words: In other words would equate the recommendation with small sample size rather than qualify the argument.

sentence: The reviewers judged the evidence insufficient. ___, the editor requested further analysis.
setupText: Choose the word presenting the action as a response consistent with the assessment, not merely a later event.
taskText: The reviewers judged the evidence insufficient. ___, the editor requested further analysis.
text: Choose the word presenting the action as a response consistent with the assessment, not merely a later event. The reviewers judged the evidence insufficient. ___, the editor requested further analysis.
options: Subsequently
Conversely
Accordingly
Meanwhile
answer: Accordingly
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-575:Accordingly versus subsequently
explanation: Accordingly connects the editorial action to the assessment that makes it appropriate.

rationales.Subsequently: Subsequently orders the events but does not explicitly show the action following from the judgment.
rationales.Conversely: Conversely introduces a reversed or contrasting relationship, not a response aligned with the judgment.
rationales.Meanwhile: Meanwhile would emphasize simultaneity rather than a response based on the assessment.
rationales.Accordingly: Accordingly connects the editorial action to the assessment that makes it appropriate.

sentence: 'The estimates remain provisional pending the completion of the independent audit.'

focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-576:Pending as a provisional temporal link
explanation: 'Pending' marks the period awaiting a specified event; the notice does not say what the audit will conclude.

rationales.The estimates retain provisional status: 'Pending' marks the period awaiting a specified event; the notice does not say what the audit will conclude.
rationales.The completed audit has already confirme: Completion is still awaited, and no confirmation is reported.
rationales.The estimates are provisional because th: The notice does not state cancellation or make it a cause.
rationales.Completion of the audit is postponed unt: This reverses which event is being awaited and which status continues meanwhile.

sentence: ___ the consultant's advice to postpone, the organizers confirmed the original date.
setupText: Choose the connector acknowledging a contrary recommendation while preserving the decision to proceed.

As a consequence of
For the purpose of
Notwithstanding
answer: Notwithstanding
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-577:Notwithstanding for acting against a conceded consideration

sentence: 'The two versions are identical, save that the revised one includes a glossary.'

The glossary is presented as the exception to their identity.

focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-578:Save that introduces a restricted exception
explanation: 'Save that' means 'except that' and isolates the added glossary as the stated difference.

rationales.The versions differ throughout because a: Save that limits the difference rather than extending it throughout the versions.
rationales.The glossary is presented as the excepti: 'Save that' means 'except that' and isolates the added glossary as the stated difference.

rationales.The versions will become identical after: The sentence compares existing versions and reports no future step toward identity.

sentence: 'The recommendation is persuasive to the extent that its cost estimates are reliable.'

focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-579:To the extent that links degrees of support
explanation: To the extent that limits persuasive force according to the degree of reliability in its basis.

rationales.The recommendation itself makes the esti: This reverses the dependency between supporting estimates and persuasive force.
rationales.The recommendation is persuasive despite: The sentence ties persuasive force to reliability, rather than conceding unreliability.
rationales.Reliability has been established beyond: The degree clause does not itself establish the estimates' actual reliability.
rationales.Its persuasive force depends on how reli: To the extent that limits persuasive force according to the degree of reliability in its basis.

sentence: 'The panel debated whether the existing evidence justified a second trial.'
setupText: Choose what the whether-clause does in the sentence.
taskText: 'The panel debated whether the existing evidence justified a second trial.'
text: Choose what the whether-clause does in the sentence. 'The panel debated whether the existing evidence justified a second trial.'
options: It states that the evidence justified a second trial.
It gives the cause of holding a second trial.
It identifies an unresolved question that the panel discussed.
It sets a condition that automatically requires another trial.
answer: It identifies an unresolved question that the panel discussed.
focusKey: coverage-clauses-and-connectors-c1-580:Whether introduces the content of a debated question
explanation: The clause supplies the content of the debate as an open yes-or-no issue.

rationales.It states that the evidence justified a: 'Whether' introduces the issue for debate, not an assertion of the positive answer.
rationales.It gives the cause of holding a second t: The sentence reports discussion and does not report a second trial being held.
rationales.It identifies an unresolved question tha: The clause supplies the content of the debate as an open yes-or-no issue.
rationales.It sets a condition that automatically r: This is an embedded question, not a rule stating a sufficient condition for a trial.
